title: Acne mimics: rosacea, steroid eruptions and folliculitis
summary: Rosacea (no comedones), steroid-induced eruptions, perioral dermatitis, and Gram-negative, Malassezia and Pseudomonas folliculitis.

glance.think: Central facial redness, flushing and papules **without comedones** in an adult — or monomorphic pustules after steroids / long antibiotics.
glance.engine: Neurovascular and innate immune dysregulation (rosacea); drug or microbiome shifts driving folliculitis variants.
glance.backbone: Rosacea: trigger avoidance, sunscreen, topical ivermectin (± oral doxycycline MR). Stop the culprit steroid or tetracycline when a mimic appears.
glance.never_miss: Rosacea fulminans (explosive central face in a young woman) and ocular keratitis — urgent ophthalmology / dermatology. Do not keep cycling antibiotics for Gram-negative folliculitis.

what: Not every facial papule is acne. This page covers the common **mimics** taught with Module 6 Week 2: **rosacea** (and rosacea fulminans), **steroid-induced** acne/rosacea/perioral dermatitis, and **folliculitis variants** (Gram-negative, Malassezia, *Pseudomonas*/hot-tub).
True acne vulgaris is covered separately: [acne vulgaris](condition:acne-vulgaris).

list: **Rosacea:** neurovascular dysregulation, innate immunity (cathelicidin), *Demodex*, UV; triggers include heat, alcohol, spicy food, hot drinks, topical steroids.
**Steroid acne / rosacea / perioral dermatitis:** oral, inhaled, topical or illicit bleaching steroids.
**Gram-negative folliculitis:** long-term oral tetracyclines for acne/rosacea → overgrowth of *Klebsiella*, *Enterobacter*, *Proteus*.
**Malassezia folliculitis:** yeast in oily follicles, often after antibiotics or steroids.
**Hot-tub folliculitis:** *Pseudomonas* in under-chlorinated spa water.
**Rosacea fulminans (pyoderma faciale):** explosive painful papules, pustules and nodules on a red swollen central face in young women; systemically well (unlike acne fulminans).
**Steroid acne:** sudden monomorphic papules/pustules on chest/back; few comedones.
**Perioral dermatitis:** papules around mouth with vermilion sparing; often after facial steroid.
**Gram-negative folliculitis:** new perinasal pustules after months of tetracycline that initially worked.
**Malassezia:** itchy monomorphic follicular pustules on chest/back.
**Hot-tub:** itchy pustules under the swimsuit line 1–4 days after spa use.

diagnosis: Clinical. Swab pustules and anterior nares (request Gram-negative culture) when acne worsens on long antibiotics. Consider ANA only if lupus is realistic. Do not diagnose rosacea if comedones dominate — rethink acne.

management.title: Rosacea in depth
management.text: Phenotypes, flushing work-up, ocular rosacea, *Demodex* and steroid-induced rosacea now have their own page: [rosacea](condition:rosacea).

list: Trigger diary, gentle skincare, daily sunscreen; **avoid topical steroids**.
Persistent erythema: topical brimonidine (warn about rebound).
Mild–moderate papulopustular: **ivermectin 1% cream** first-line, or azelaic acid 15%, or metronidazole 0.75%.
Moderate–severe: topical ivermectin **plus** oral **doxycycline 40 mg MR** (licensed) or other tetracycline; erythromycin if tetracyclines unsuitable.
Ocular: lid hygiene, lubricants ± oral tetracycline; **same-day ophthalmology** for pain, photophobia or reduced vision.
Stop the topical/inhaled facial steroid exposure (taper systemic steroids with the original prescriber — never abruptly).
Warn of a rebound flare. Topical metronidazole or azelaic acid; oral tetracycline 6–8 weeks if needed (erythromycin if under 12).

management: Perioral dermatitis now has its own page: [Perioral dermatitis](condition:perioral-dermatitis).

list: Gram-negative: **stop the tetracycline**; swab; specialist options include isotretinoin or culture-guided antibiotics — refer rather than endless antibiotic switches.
Malassezia: topical or oral antifungal per local practice; stop unnecessary antibiotics/steroids.
Hot-tub: usually self-limiting in days; antibiotics only if severe or immunocompromised.
**Urgent dermatology referral.** Do not keep cycling oral antibiotics. Specialist care often uses a short steroid course then isotretinoin (pregnancy exclusions apply).

management.title: Check BNF
management.text: Confirm doses, pregnancy advice and interactions before prescribing.

red_flags: Ocular pain, photophobia or reduced vision → same-day ophthalmology.
Rosacea fulminans or suspected acne fulminans → urgent dermatology.
Phyma needing procedural treatment; diagnostic doubt.
Acne worsening on long tetracyclines → culture for Gram-negatives; stop the antibiotic.
pearls: **No comedones + flushing + central face = rosacea until proven otherwise.**
Maintenance topical therapy is often needed — rosacea is relapsing.
Pharmacists often spot inhaled-steroid perioral dermatitis — advise rinsing/wiping the face after inhalers.
Laser/IPL for telangiectasia is usually private, not NHS-funded.
For the full rosacea ladder by phenotype, see [rosacea](condition:rosacea).
